channel.title: The Fix Shelf — Printables & Guides
channel.description: Printable planners, logs and workbooks with how-to guides that help real life run on paper.

item.title: Weekly Meal Planner Printable with Grocery List: 7 Dinners, Aisle-Sorted List & 10-Meal Rotation
item.description: Most meal planners stop at the plan, which is why the shopping trip never matches it. This printable puts the week's 7 dinners and the grocery list on one spread — the list sorted by aisle, a 10-meal rotation so you stop reinventing the week, and space for the budget note. Print it, plan Sunday, shop once. The kitchen already has its log — the sourdough starter keeps its own feeding record — and the money side pairs with the monthly money reset, where the food plan meets the budget.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Car Maintenance Log Printable: Service Schedule by Mileage, 18-Row Service Log & Fuel Tracker
item.description: A car's service history shouldn't live in a shoebox of receipts. This printable maintenance log keeps the service schedule by mileage, an 18-row log for every visit, and a fuel tracker — so the "when was the last oil change" question has one answer, and the resale conversation has one page to show. Print it once, keep it for the life of the car.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Tax Prep Document Checklist Printable: The Four Sweeps, Freelancer Extras & 4-Week Plan
item.description: Tax season stress is almost entirely a document-hunt: receipts in three places, one missing statement, a deduction claimed with no paper behind it. This checklist runs the hunt as four sweeps, spread across four calm weeks. A single dreaded "taxes day" fails because it mixes four different kinds of hunting. One sweep a week keeps each session short and single-purpose — and by the time the deadline is close, everything is already in the folder and the only job left is the filing itself. Printable PDF, instant download.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Savings Challenge Printable Pack: 100 Envelope Challenge, 52-Week Ladder & Color-In Trackers
item.description: Named savings challenges die when the tracking is a chore — this pack puts both big ones on paper. The 100-envelope challenge gets its full grid, the 52-week ladder gets its rungs, and every tracker colors in so progress is something you can see. Print a page, pick your challenge, and start this week. Building the bigger money picture? The monthly money reset keeps the month on plan, the debt payoff tracker works the other side of the ledger, and the printable expense tracker feeds both.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Reading Journal Printable: 12-Book Challenge Grid, Book Log, Quotes & TBR List
item.description: Finishing twelve books deserves more than a mental high-five. This printable reading journal tracks the 12-book challenge on a color-in grid, logs every title, keeps the quotes worth keeping, and holds the TBR list so the next pick is already chosen. Gift-friendly for the reader in your life — including you. A log records titles and dates; a journal keeps what the books left behind — quotes, reactions, the year's thread. This printable does both: the log for the record, quote pages and TBR space.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: New Baby Bundle Printable: First Trimester Checklist + Baby Registry + Postpartum Recovery
item.description: A baby arrives in three phases and most parents buy a plan for one of them: the registry guide for the stuff, maybe a pregnancy checklist, and nothing at all for the weeks after the birth. This bundle plans all three phases, in order. The first trimester checklist runs while everything is new; the registry guide lands in month four or five when the stuff decisions peak; the recovery checklist is printed and ready before the due date, because nobody plans the fourth trimester from a hospital bed. Printable PDF, instant download.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Monthly Habit Tracker Printable: 31-Day Grid, Streak Insurance & the Never-Miss-Twice Rule
item.description: Most habit trackers punish the missed day with a blank that kills the streak and then the habit. This printable monthly tracker runs a 31-day grid per habit, adds streak insurance for the days life happens, and builds in the never-miss-twice rule — miss once, fine; miss twice, that's the pattern. ADHD-friendly design leads; everyone else is welcome.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Medication Tracker Printable: Household Med List, Daily Check-off Grid & Refill Tracker
item.description: When several people in a house take several things, the question "did they take it?" gets answered from memory — badly. This printable medication tracker keeps one household med list, a daily check-off grid for the whole week, and a refill tracker so the empty-box surprise stops happening. Bring the log to appointments instead of a guess. Informational only — not medical advice.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: House Cleaning Schedule Printable: 15 Minutes a Day, Weekly Zones & Monthly Deep Tasks
item.description: Whole-house cleaning fails because it waits for a free Saturday that never comes. This printable schedule splits it: 15 minutes a day, one weekly zone at a time, and the deep tasks — vents, fridge, windows — on a monthly rotation so nothing is only cleaned when company comes. Print it, stick it inside a cabinet door, stop renegotiating with yourself.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Homeschool Planner Printable: Year Map, Weekly Lesson Grids & the Attendance Log
item.description: Homeschool records live in eleven places until inspection week makes that expensive. This printable planner keeps the year map, weekly lesson grids and the attendance log in one binder: plan the year once, run each week on a grid, and the records question is already answered. Built for the family that actually files things.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Home Management Binder Printable: Moving Planner + Maintenance Calendar + Emergency Binder
item.description: Three documents decide how well a house is run: the plan that gets you moved in without chaos, the calendar that keeps the house maintained instead of repaired, and the binder that has everything findable when something goes wrong. This Homeowners Bundle is all three, together — the whole life of a house on paper. The moving planner gets you in; the maintenance calendar keeps the house ahead of its repairs; the emergency binder means that if the water main goes at 2am, the shut-off map is on a known shelf, not in a drawer nobody has opened since move-in. Printable PDF, instant download.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Family Chore Chart Printable Pack: Age Lists, Weekly Rotation & the Points System
item.description: "Whose turn is it" is a daily argument because the answer lives in nobody's head. This printable pack puts it on the wall: age-appropriate chore lists for kids, teens and adults, a weekly rotation so the same child doesn't always get the bins, and a points system that makes follow-through visible. One pack, every age in the house.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Expense Tracker Printable: Daily Capture Log, Category Totals & the Weekly Check
item.description: Budgets fail at the daily level — the coffee, the parking, the thing that was "basically free." This printable expense tracker captures spending the day it happens, totals it by category, and runs the weekly five-minute check so the month never gets away. For the full paper money system: the monthly money reset plans the month, the debt payoff tracker aims it, the tax prep checklist reads this log at tax time, and the savings challenge pack takes the spare dollars once the totals are honest.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Debt Payoff Tracker Printable: Avalanche & Snowball Plans, 12-Month Log, Debt-Free Date
item.description: Paying off debt fails quietly, not dramatically: payments go out, the balances drift down, and there's no visible progress to keep the motivation fed. This tracker puts the whole payoff on paper — the plan, the log, and the date. On pure maths, avalanche wins — kill the highest interest rate and every dollar works harder. On human maths, snowball wins more often — the early killed balances are the motivation that keeps the plan alive at month four. The tracker lays both out with your real numbers so the choice is yours and visible. Printable PDF, instant download.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Christmas Planner Printable: 6-Week Countdown, Gift Budget Tracker & Food Plan
item.description: Christmas doesn't go wrong on the day — it goes wrong in the six weeks before it, quietly: gifts bought at panic prices, the food shop duplicated, the budget a mystery until the January statement. This planner runs the whole six weeks on paper. Six weeks is the window where Christmas is still cheap: gifts bought in November cost less and ship calmly, food can be bought across several normal shops instead of one panic trip, and nothing needs a rush fee. Starting at six weeks is what makes the countdown gentle instead of frantic. Printable PDF, instant download.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: ADHD Weekly Planner: The Sunday Reset That Actually Sticks
item.description: Most planners fail adult ADHD brains for a boring reason: they're designed by and for people whose brains cooperate. The Weekly Reset flips the design — one page, one sitting, and a Sunday routine that takes about an hour. Monday-morning planning collides with the hardest executive-function moment of the week. Planning on Sunday, when the pressure is off, means decisions are already made when Monday shows up. The reset walks you through four moves:
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Wedding Planning Checklist Printable: 12 Months, 12 Short Lists
item.description: Nine to twelve months out, the advice online adds up to one 300-item monster list — which is exactly the kind of list nobody works through. This version is scoped differently: each month owns a handful of decisions, and the checklist tells you what to stop thinking about until its month arrives. Start at your month, ignore everything before it.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Wedding Day Timeline Template: Hour-by-Hour for 2pm, 3pm & 4pm Ceremonies
item.description: Pick your ceremony time below, copy the table, and adjust three variables: photo time, travel between sites, and sunset. These are workable defaults built to survive a 20-minute delay — not rigid schedules. For most weddings, hair and makeup start 3–4 hours before the ceremony for the couple, and the wedding party joins about 90 minutes in. The buffer isn't beauty time — it absorbs the delayed makeup artist, the missing groomsman and the "just one more photo" that always happens.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: Vegetable Garden Planner Printable: Bed Maps, Calendar & Season Log
item.description: Most garden "planning" is a planting list — and planting lists fail by July, because a list doesn't say what goes where, when it goes in, or what actually produced last year. A garden plan that gets used has three parts: a map, a calendar, and a log. Here's how each one works on paper. A list tells you what to buy. A map tells you what goes where — and prevents planting the shade-lover behind the six-foot tomatoes. A calendar tells you when, anchored to your frost dates. The log is the part everyone skips and the part that compounds: it's the reason year three is better than year one. Lists alone fail because they answer none of the three questions that actually decide a season.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf

item.title: How to Reset a Messed Up Sleep Schedule (Honest Timeline + Method)
item.description: Your sleep slid to 3am and the mornings are wrecked, and the internet keeps promising fixes "in one day." Here's the honest version: how fast you recover depends on how far you drifted, the method is the same either way, and one bad night doesn't undo the work. Plain line first — this is routine-building, not medical advice; if you suspect a sleep disorder, see a doctor.
item.dc:creator: The Fix Shelf
